subject: Re: Migration mode selection — deployment mode recommendation & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@novahealth.com>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@novahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment mode options — follow-up and recommended next steps

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the call today — great discussion on Nova Health's roadmap and the constraints you mentioned around PHI handling, latency for clinician workflows, and current spend on your self-hosted cluster. Quick recap and recommended path: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Current setup: Legacy GPU cluster running a mix of open models and proprietary prompts; significant ops burden and unpredictable latency under load.
- Requirements: PHI-safe processing, SOC2 evidence for procurement, sub-200ms median response for triage flows, predictable monthly cost.
- Constraints: Data residency (US only), procurement window targeting Sept budget approval.

Redwood recommendation (short + medium term):
1) Short pilot: Hosted Redwood API for a narrow set of triage endpoints (fast to spin up, no infra procurement) — 2–4 week pilot to validate latency and prompt-quality.
2) Medium-term (production): Dedicated capacity with reserved GPU pool in a US region — meets performance/SLA and predictable pricing.
3) Private VPC/on-prem: Option if procurement/legal requires customer-managed network and HSM; longer lead time (8–12 weeks) and higher fixed costs.

Attached: redwood-deployment-comparison-v2.pdf (summary matrix), and a draft mutual-action-plan we can iterate.

Proposed next steps:
- You: confirm which two triage endpoints you'd like in the pilot (we can run with sample data or synthetic).
- We: scope the Hosted API pilot and share an SOW + estimated pricing by EOD Friday.
- If you prefer, we can schedule a deep-dive with Aditya (solutions eng) to review latency and model selection.

Would you like Aditya looped in now or after you confirm the pilot endpoints?

Best,
Marissa
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0146

Attachments: redwood-deployment-comparison-v2.pdf, mutual-action-plan-nh.xlsx

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A couple notes / clarifications from our side: 

- Pilot endpoints: 1) Intake triage (classify incoming messages into urgency buckets), 2) Discharge summary summarization (de-identification then summarize).
- PHI handling: we need to ensure we can either bring data in encrypted form and have logs showing access; procurement will push for SOC2 artefacts before signing anything.
- Latency: target is 200ms p50 for triage when batched at ~8 concurrent requests; peak hourly QPS could spike to ~120.

Pilot preference: we like the Hosted API pilot to validate quality while procurement works through SOC2 questions. If Hosted shows we can hit latency, procurement will fast-track Dedicated.

Please loop Aditya for the latency/throughput discussion. Also please share the SOC2 evidence you referenced.

—Alex

Hi all — thanks, Marissa. Quick pilot/test plan and recommendations below.

Pilot objective: validate latency and quality on Hosted API, unblock procurement with SOC2 artifacts, and produce signal to justify Dedicated capacity if the Hosted pilot meets SLOs.

Test plan (3 phases):
1) Smoke (2 business days) — basic functionality for both endpoints with small synthetic corpus. Confirm correctness and logging.
2) Load & latency (3 business days) — ramp to 8 concurrent active requests and run 1-hour sustained window; measure p50/p95/p99. Also run spike test to 120 QPS for 10 minutes to observe graceful degradation.
3) Production-sim (3 business days) — run day-long window with mixed payload sizes matching Nova's distribution; collect cost telemetry and KV/prefix cache hit rates.

Model & infra suggestions:
- Triage: quantized LLM (e.g., 8-bit optimized) on Hosted API with continuous batching enabled — expected p50 ~120–160ms for 8 concurrent requests depending on prompt size.
- Summarization: mid-size model with stronger decoding for quality; p50 will be higher but acceptable for non-real-time workflows.

Data handling / SOC2:
- We'll provide SOC2 artifact pack (SOC2-evidence-request.pdf) and a short writeup on PHI flow for the Hosted pilot. Logs include request/response metadata; for PHI, recommend using de-identified payloads for pilot and encrypted payloads for later stages.

Deliverables & timeline:
- Pilot plan + load scripts (this email + attachments) — today
- Hosted Pilot SOW + pricing (Stephanie) — Wed 18 Aug
- Pilot kickoff (if dates align) — target Mon 23 Aug

Action items:
- Alex/Priya: confirm synthetic vs de-identified for pilot payloads and pick pilot window.
- Stephanie: finalize SOW and include an option for a Dedicated capacity quote if pilot meets SLOs.

I'll be available for a 30-min call to walk through the load tests if helpful.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
